chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

the person in ihram who has intercourse with his wife, he said: 'If he has fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel (badanah) and he must repeat the hajj next year. And if he has not fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel and he is not required to repeat the hajj next year.' And that which indicates the observance of the second condition in the repetition of the hajj, which is that the intercourse occurred before the standing (at Arafat), is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْوُقُوفُ: The standing at Arafat (a key pillar of hajj)
key_terms.اَلْحَجُّ مِنْ قَابِلٍ: The hajj repeated the following year
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (specific type of sacrificial animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation for a pilgrim who has sexual intercourse before and after the standing at Arafat?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific expiation for a pilgrim in *ihram* who engages in sexual intercourse with his spouse, distinguishing between full penetration (*afda*) and partial contact. The ruling mandates offering a camel (*badanah*) in both cases, but only full penetration necessitates repeating the Hajj the following year, a distinction rooted in the condition of the act occurring before the standing at Arafat. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the degree of intimacy in determining the severity of the ritual penalty.
